context:
Goal: a runner cannot merge a lower-priority PR ahead of a ready top-priority PR (the #3302 sequence), and the check that stops it is not switched off by a permission prompt.
Problem (rule): the new check adds a flag, --priority-rows <file>, to the runner's merge command. Two settings.json allow entries ("Relayed Merge Yes" and "Batch Runner Merge", lines 59-60) name the allowed act as `merge <pr> --confirm --head <sha>` and say any other act is not covered. The auto-mode classifier may read the new flag as a different act and deny the runner's call. Nobody could probe the classifier. Only you change permission settings.
Based on (read): the lane's round 2 reviewer, settings.json:59-60, operating-model.md runner confirm forms; relayed by the lane priority-vs-merge-order (session_013NEJKzPki46QeHmV8zxLAh) 23:56 CST; unchecked by triage. Your earlier picks on allow entries (759 b, 753 a, the reinstall entry) each named one exact act; none covers this flag.
Departs from: main — the two entries name `--confirm --head <sha>` only; a adds `[--priority-rows <file>]` to both; b leaves them.
Meanwhile: the lane continues round 3; the check is built; nothing else depends on this.
home: lane priority-vs-merge-order (branch priority-vs-merge-order); settings.json autoMode.allow lines 59-60; its pinned test hooks/test_auto_mode_allow.py
lastAnswer: 817: a, extend both allow entries (00:19 CST Nov 14).

options.gain: The runner's gated merge is covered and the check runs.
options.how: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo
options.label: Extend both allow entries to name `merge <pr> --confirm --head <sha> [--priority-rows <file>]`
options.lose: The allow entry names one more form (a read-only gate flag on the same act); the pinned test changes with it.

options.gain: No settings change; your rule against widening stays.
options.label: Leave the entries; the lane hands in marked "classifier unknown" and runner 10 reports a denial if one occurs (recommended by triage)
options.lose: A denied call may push runners to leave the flag off, which turns the check off.

reply: Closed on your a. Filed as ruling own-817-a-priority-rows. Both allow entries name the optional --priority-rows flag, nothing else. Lane priority-vs-merge-order changes settings.json by draft PR, with its pinned test.
short: Allow the --priority-rows flag in the runner's merge entries?
title: The new priority check adds a flag to the runner's merge command. Add it to the two allow entries (a), or leave them and see if it is denied (b)?
why: Only you change permission settings, and a denied call could switch the check off.
